SMTO-EXE-0048 — SMTO couldn't confirm the earlier job has stopped

GUID: 2804e386-ffdf-4287-a619-d2fa8b4f2c89
Slug: resource-reset-termination-unverified
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: exe

What happened

  • SMTO tried to stop an earlier job that was in the way, but it couldn't confirm the job really ended. SMTO keeps treating it as possibly running, and your command still hasn't run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait about a minute, then read the recovery card's status line in the task. A stopped program can take a little time to close, and the card shows its latest state.
  2. If the card now offers Wait until the job state changes, select it, or select Resolve forcefully by terminating job again if it is still offered. SMTO will only continue once it can confirm the earlier job has really ended.
  3. Before asking SMTO to redo anything, check the file, service or machine the earlier job was changing to see what it already did. The earlier job may have kept running for a while, so its changes might already be in place.
  4. Ask the person who manages the Gateway computer to check whether the earlier command is still running there. Someone on that computer can see whether the program is really still running.

What success looks like

  • The recovery card shows that the earlier job has ended and the task continues.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway computer. Don't end other programs on that computer and don't ask SMTO to repeat the earlier change until they confirm the job has stopped.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway sent a forced stop to the recorded blocking process during reset, but afterwards it still saw the process alive, could not prove it had exited, or the blocker had no process identity and no eligible reset basis (resource_reset_termination_unverified).

What this means

  • After reset control, the Gateway still observed the recorded process alive, could not prove its death, or lacked identity with no eligible reset basis. Sending termination did not satisfy the postcondition. Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.

Why this can happen

  • After reset control, the Gateway still observed the recorded process alive, could not prove its death, or lacked identity with no eligible reset basis. Sending termination did not satisfy the postcondition.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect exact PID plus creation identity, retained reset decision and current liveness; preserve claims while termination remains unverified.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the recorded command_pid and supervisor identity and the current job status on the Gateway. Leave the resource claims in place until the reset flow verifies termination or explicitly records the allowed unknown-identity case; do not signal a different PID or treat a missing reply as proof that the process ended.
  • Inspect the exact recorded process identity and current job status. Preserve its resource claims until the supported control flow verifies termination or explicitly records the permitted unknown state.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • The owning reset flow proves the required termination or explicitly settles the permitted unknown-identity case before releasing claims.

What not to do

  • Do not infer successful termination from a missing response, target another PID, or replay the blocked operation.

Technical notes

  • Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
